title: Counting the Scenery: How Foraging Honeybees Gauge Distance from Optic Flow
abstract: A forager that returns to the hive reports how far away the food lies through the duration of its waggle dance. We trained honeybees to feeders between 50 and 400 m from the hive across an open meadow, and through short tunnels lined with different patterns. Over open ground the waggle run grew steadily with distance. In a tunnel with a dense checkerboard lining, a flight of a few metres was reported as a journey of hundreds, whereas a tunnel with axial stripes left the dance almost unchanged. In this illustrative study the bees’ odometer reads image motion, not effort.
